mainTopic: Mixing the נסכים of different קרבנות, the עומר lamb's נסכים, and an offering slaughtered שלא לשמו that keeps its special requirements
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about mixing the נסכים of different קרבנות. נסכים with the same oil-to-flour ratio may be mixed, but lamb נסכים may not be mixed with bull or ram נסכים. The משנה also teaches that the lamb brought with the עומר has double flour but not double oil and wine. The גמרא points out that a ברייתא forbids mixing the parts of different offerings, which seems to contradict the משנה. רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה speaks only after the fact. The גמרא shows from the משנה's structure that this does not work. אביי then explains that wine may be mixed, except when the flour and oil are still separate and unburned. Next, a ברייתא and רבי אלעזר derive from 'ונסכה' (as written) and 'ונסכו' (as read) that the עומר lamb's oil, like its wine, stays a quarter הין. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו still needs נסכים. רב מנשיא בר גדא challenges this from the עומר lamb and the תמיד. אביי answers that רבי יוחנן gave only one example, and רבי אבא begins a different answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Today's libations may be mixed with yesterday's
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of permitted mixtures: נסכים from today's offering may be mixed with נסכים from yesterday's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may mix the libations of today's offering with those of yesterday's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last item in the משנה's list of libations that may be mixed together. Libations from an offering brought today may be mixed with libations from an offering brought the day before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the ratio of oil to flour, not when the offering was brought. If the two meal offerings have the same ratio, the different days make no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations: the flour-and-oil meal offering and the wine that come along with an animal offering
One may mix together
Yesterday, the day before

phrases.english: [And one may mix the libations] of today with those of yesterday.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁל יוֹם בְּשֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of permitted mixtures from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Libations of today's offering may be mixed with libations of yesterday's offering.

steps.title: Lamb libations may not be mixed with bull or ram libations
steps.stepSummary: Lamb libations may not be mixed with bull or ram libations. But if each was already mixed with its own oil first, a later mix-up leaves them כשר. If they got mixed before that, they are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may not mix the libations of lambs with the libations of bulls and rams. If each kind was already mixed with its oil on its own and only then they got mixed together, they are fit. If they got mixed before the mixing of flour and oil was done, they are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit: lamb libations cannot be combined with bull or ram libations. It then explains what happens if they do get mixed by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb's meal offering uses more oil for each measure of flour than a bull's or a ram's, so mixing them would throw off the amounts. If each was already mixed with its own oil, it has the right amount and stays כשר. If they were mixed before that, the oil is spread out at the wrong ratio, so they become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing the flour with its oil to make the meal offering
They became mixed together
Fit, valid for the altar
Disqualified, invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Two different kinds of 'mixing' are going on here. בְּלִילָה means mixing flour with its own oil. נִתְעָרְבוּ means two separate offerings getting mixed with each other. Everything depends on which one happened first.

phrases.english: But one may not mix the libations of lambs
with the libations of bulls and rams,
and if one mixed [flour and oil of] these by themselves
and those by themselves, and then they got mixed together – they are fit,
if [they got mixed] before he mixed [flour and oil] – it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין מְעָרְבִין נִסְכֵי כְבָשִׂים בְּנִסְכֵי פָרִים וְאֵילִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the permitted mixtures listed in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lamb libations may not be mixed with bull or ram libations. After the fact, they are כשר if each was mixed with its own oil first, and פסול if they were mixed together before that.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the key factor is the correct oil-to-flour ratio. This is exactly the idea the גמרא is about to challenge.

steps.title: The lamb of the עומר gets double flour but not double libations
steps.stepSummary: The lamb brought with the עומר has a double portion of flour in its meal offering, but its oil and wine are not doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lamb that comes with the עומר: even though its meal offering is doubled, its libations were not doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches a special rule for the lamb brought together with the עומר. Its flour is double the normal amount, but its oil and wine stay at the regular amount for a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the amounts of oil and wine go up along with the flour. Here only the flour is doubled. The oil and wine stay at the normal lamb amount, three לוג each.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן
A lamb (here, the burnt offering brought with the עומר)
Its meal offering is doubled: two tenths of flour instead of one

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר lamb has double flour, but its oil and wine are the normal amount for a lamb.

phrases.english: The lamb that comes with the omer,
even though its meal offering is doubled –
phrases.notes: The doubling refers to the flour: two tenths of an איפה instead of the usual one tenth for a lamb.

phrases.english: its libations were not doubled.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֶּבֶשׂ הַבָּא עִם הָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new rule in the משנה about the amounts of libations
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר lamb's flour is doubled, but its oil and wine libations remain the standard lamb amount.

steps.title: The גמרא sets up a contradiction to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and announces that it will raise a contradiction to the משנה's rule allowing libations to be mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And raise a contradiction against it:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting, and this line is only a setup. It tells us a contradiction to the משנה is coming, and the source itself will be quoted in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ורמינהו signals that another source seems to disagree with the משנה. The target is the משנה's rule that different offerings' libations may be mixed together. The actual challenge has not been quoted yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
And raise a contradiction: another source is placed against this one

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And raise a contradiction:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה by preparing a contradiction
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that libations of different offerings may be mixed together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source will be brought that seems to require each offering to be kept separate, which would clash with the משנה. This line only sets up that challenge.

steps.title: The ברייתא: offerings' parts should not be mixed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the singular word והקטירו ('and he shall burn it') that one may not mix the fats of one offering with the fats of another. The same should apply to libations, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall burn it' teaches that one should not mix fats with fats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source it set up in step 4. A ברייתא says each offering's parts must be burned on their own, not mixed with another offering's parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses a singular 'it' even though many fats are listed, so each offering is handled by itself. If fats may not be mixed, libations should not be mixed either. That clashes with the משנה, which allows mixing libations.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall burn it (singular 'it')
The fats of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
That one should not mix

phrases.english: "And he shall burn it"
teaches that one should not mix fats with fats.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְהִקְטִירוֹ״, שֶׁלֹּא יְעָרֵב חֲלָבִים בַּחֲלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction announced in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling (step 1) that libations of different offerings may be mixed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse shows that each offering's parts must stay separate, so mixing libations should be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the משנה means only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה never allowed mixing from the start. It only means that if the libations already got mixed, they are still fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the משנה is saying 'if they got mixed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction. The משנה is talking about after the fact, while the ברייתא is talking about what to do from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids mixing from the start (לכתחילה). The משנה only says that libations which already got mixed may still be offered (בדיעבד). The two sources describe different stages, so they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: They got mixed (already happened)
From the start, before acting
After the fact

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is saying "if they got mixed."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: ״אִם נִתְעָרְבוּ״ קָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה as speaking בדיעבד, not לכתחילה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows mixing libations from the start, against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only rules that libations which got mixed remain valid.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows its start is about לכתחילה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is only about after the fact, then its ban on mixing lamb libations with bull or ram libations would mean they are invalid even after the fact. But the משנה's last clause separately discusses the after-the-fact case, which shows the first clause is about לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, when the משנה says one may not mix lamb libations with bull and ram libations, does it mean that even if they got mixed they are invalid? But since the last clause teaches that if each was mixed with its own flour and oil and then they got mixed, they are valid, it follows that the first clause speaks about what one may do from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. His reading does not fit the way the משנה is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole משנה is about 'after the fact,' then 'one may not mix lamb with bull libations' would mean they are invalid even after the fact. But the סיפא spells out an after-the-fact case on its own (step 2). That shows the רישא is about לכתחילה, so the משנה's permission to mix must also be לכתחילה, and the contradiction comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (testing what follows from the answer)
The first clause
The last clause
It follows from this
He mixed them (the flour with the oil)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two kinds of 'mixing.' בְּלָלָן means mixing flour with oil to prepare the offering. נִתְעָרְבוּ means the two offerings' parts got mixed with each other.

phrases.english: If so,
then 'one may not mix libations of lambs'
with libations of bulls and rams'
would mean that even if they got mixed, they are also not valid?
But since the last clause teaches:
if he mixed these by themselves
and those by themselves
and then they got mixed together, they are valid,
it follows that the first clause
is speaking about what to do from the start!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין נִסְכֵי כְבָשִׂים בְּנִסְכֵי פָרִים וְאֵילִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה speaks only בדיעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא covers the after-the-fact case on its own, so the רישא must be about לכתחילה. The משנה's language is therefore לכתחילה language.

steps.title: אביי: the wine may be mixed from the start
steps.stepSummary: אביי rereads the משנה. The wine libations may be mixed from the start, and the 'if they got mixed' part refers to the flour and oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is what it means. We may mix their wine, if their flour and oil were already mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer that keeps the משנה's words as לכתחילה. He splits the libation into its wine on one side and its flour and oil on the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixing the wine of different offerings is allowed from the start. The 'if they got mixed' wording is about the flour and oil, which were already mixed together. This keeps the רישא as לכתחילה language, which answers the challenge in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading)
Their wine
Their fine flour
Their oil

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads the משנה as only after the fact, but the משנה's structure rules that out. אביי's first reading here is challenged in the next step, and he replaces it with a fuller reading in step 10.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This is what it is saying:
we may mix their wine,
if their flour and their oil were mixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 with a new reading, replacing רבי יוחנן's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the libation: wine on one side, flour and oil on the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is only after the fact (רבי יוחנן), which its structure does not allow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine may be mixed לכתחילה, and 'if they got mixed' refers to the flour and oil.

steps.title: A ברייתא says wine may be mixed from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's reading. A ברייתא says the ban on mixing applies only to flour and oil, while wine may be mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that their wine may not be mixed from the start? But a ברייתא teaches: when is this rule said? Only for flour and oil. But wine, one may mix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's reading from Step 8. That reading tied the mixing of the wine to the flour and oil, but a ברייתא seems to allow mixing wine with no conditions at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reading suggested there are times when wine may not be mixed לכתחילה. The ברייתא limits the ban to flour and oil and allows wine outright. So אביי's reading seems too strict about the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? A phrase that limits a rule to certain cases
Fine flour and oil, the parts of the מנחה that go with the offering

phrases.english: And their wine may not be mixed from the start?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: These words point back to the ban on mixing parts of different offerings, from Step 5.

phrases.english: With flour and oil,
but wine, one may mix.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵינָן לְכִתְחִלָּה לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reading of the משנה from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading, which allows mixing the wine only when certain conditions are met
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the ban to flour and oil and allows wine outright, so wine should be mixable from the start in every case.

steps.title: אביי's new reading explains when wine may be mixed
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that wine may be mixed from the start once the flour and oil are burned or already mixed. If neither happened, the wine is not mixed, so people will not come to mix flour and oil from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: this is what it means. Where their flour and oil were already burned, one may mix the wine from the start. Where they were not burned: if their flour and oil got mixed, one may also mix their wine. If not, one may not mix, because a person might come to mix flour and oil from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops his earlier reading and gives a new one that fits the ברייתא. Mixing wine is fine in most cases, with one exception that exists only to protect the flour and oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine itself is not forbidden to mix, which is why the ברייתא can say 'wine, one may mix.' The only time we hold back is when the flour and oil are still separate and not yet burned. Mixing the wine then might lead someone to mix the flour and oil too, and that really is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Was burned on the מזבח
Got mixed, after the fact
Perhaps he will come to...; a worry that one act will lead to a forbidden one

steps.whatToRemember: Wine of different offerings may be mixed. The exception is when the flour and oil are still separate and unburned, because mixing the wine might lead to mixing the flour and oil.
steps.confusionAlert: The ban on wine here is not because wine itself cannot be mixed. It is only a protective rule for the flour and oil.

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said:
This is what it is saying:
Where their flour and their oil were burned,
one may mix the wine from the start.
Where it was not burned,
if their flour and their oil got mixed,
one may also mix their wine,
and if not, one may not mix,
lest he come to mix
flour and oil from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Step 9 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה, with a protective rule (גזירה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine may be mixed only if the flour and oil were mixed, which clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine is basically allowed to be mixed. It is held back only when the flour and oil are still separate and unburned, to prevent mixing them.

steps.title: The מנחה of the lamb brought with the עומר is doubled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next topic in the משנה, the lamb brought with the עומר. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that its מנחה is two עשרונים, double the usual amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the lamb that comes with the עומר, רבנן taught: 'And its מנחה shall be two עשרונים.' This teaches that the lamb brought with the עומר has a doubled מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the rule. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb normally comes with a מנחה of one עשרון of flour. The פסוק about the עומר's lamb says 'two עשרונים,' so this lamb's מנחה is double.

keyTerms.meaning: The lamb brought as an עולה together with the עומר offering on the sixteenth of ניסן
Tenths of an איפה, a measure of flour
Doubled

phrases.english: The lamb that comes with the עומר:
The Rabbis taught:
"And its meal offering shall be two tenths"

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל כֶּבֶשׂ הַבָּא עִם הָעוֹמֶר
phrases.english: this teaches about the lamb that comes with the עומר
that its meal offering is doubled.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֶּבֶשׂ הַבָּא עִם הָעוֹמֶר, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחה of the lamb brought with the עומר is two עשרונים, double the usual amount.

steps.title: Should the wine be doubled too?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that since the מנחה is doubled, maybe the wine is doubled as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: just as its מנחה is doubled, so too its wine is doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea, using the standard 'יכול' (you might think) style, so that it can reject it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the amounts of flour, oil and wine go up together. So it seems logical that if the flour is doubled, the wine would be doubled too, from a quarter הין to a half הין.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think'; it raises an idea the ברייתא is about to reject
Wine, poured as a נסך on the מזבח

phrases.english: One might think: just as its meal offering is doubled,
so too its wine is doubled?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמִּנְחָתוֹ כְּפוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the doubling from Step 11 also applies to the wine.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wine of the עומר's lamb is doubled like its מנחה.

steps.title: The פסוק says the wine stays a quarter הין
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק itself says the wine is a quarter הין, the normal amount for a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'And its נסך, wine, a quarter of a הין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question straight from the same פסוק. The wine is not doubled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A quarter הין is the regular wine amount for a lamb. Since the פסוק names that amount for this lamb, only the flour is doubled, not the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches'; it brings a פסוק to settle the question
A quarter of a הין, the regular נסכים amount for a lamb
Its libation

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And its libation shall be of wine, a quarter of the hin."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְנִסְכּוֹ יַיִן רְבִיעִית הַהִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wine is not doubled. It stays a quarter הין.

steps.title: Maybe the oil should be doubled, since it is mixed into the flour
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that the oil might be different from the wine. The oil is mixed into the flour, so maybe it is doubled along with the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the wine is not doubled because it is not mixed with the מנחה, but the oil should be doubled because it is mixed with the מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new possible idea that splits the oil from the wine, and it will reject this idea next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine is poured on its own, so it makes sense that it is not tied to the flour's amount. The oil, however, is kneaded into the flour, so maybe more flour needs more oil.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed in with, like oil kneaded into flour
Oil mixed into the flour of the מנחה

phrases.english: One might think its wine should not be doubled
because it is not mixed in with its meal offering,
but its oil should be doubled
because it is mixed in with its meal offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהֵא יֵינוֹ כָּפוּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִבְלָל עִם מִנְחָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the wine is not doubled (Step 13) but asks whether the oil is different.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the oil, which is mixed into the doubled flour, is doubled too.

steps.title: All the נסכים stay a quarter הין, oil included
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ונסכו' (its libation) covers all the liquids, oil as well as wine. So none of them is doubled, and they all stay a quarter הין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches 'and its נסך': all of its נסכים shall be only a quarter הין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea that the oil is doubled and gives its final rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ונסכו' is read as including every liquid that comes with the lamb, not just the wine. So even though the oil is mixed into the doubled flour, it stays at a quarter הין.

keyTerms.meaning: Its libations, meaning all its liquids: wine and oil

steps.whatToRemember: The lamb brought with the עומר has a doubled מנחה of flour, but its oil and its wine are not doubled. Both stay a quarter הין.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "And its libation":
all of its libations shall be nothing
but a quarter.
phrases.notes: He means a quarter of a הין, the same amount named in the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר וְנִסְכּוֹ כׇּל נְסָכָיו לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea in Step 14 and closes the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only the flour of the עומר lamb's מנחה is doubled. All its נסכים, oil and wine, stay a quarter הין.

steps.title: Where exactly is this learned from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word 'ונסכו' teaches that the oil is not doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source in the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא's last proof works. It is setting up רבי אלעזר's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'ונסכו' covers the oil too, but the plain word 'libation' sounds like it is only about wine. The גמרא wants to know what in the פסוק ties the oil to the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: The source or derivation; how the law is learned from the פסוק

phrases.english: What is the derivation?
phrases.notes: He is asking how the word 'ונסכו' from the ברייתא in Step 15 proves that the oil stays a quarter הין.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the ברייתא's conclusion in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word 'ונסכו' includes the oil and limits it to a quarter הין.

steps.title: Written one way, read another way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that the word is written 'ונסכה' (feminine) but read 'ונסכו' (masculine).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: It is written 'ונסכה' (her libation), and we read it as 'ונסכו' (his libation).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers by pointing to a spelling detail in the פסוק. The written word and the way we read it out loud are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Written with a ה at the end, the word is feminine and refers to the מנחה, so 'its libation' means the oil mixed into it. Read with a ו, it is masculine and refers to the lamb, so 'its libation' means the wine. One word points at both liquids together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written; the spelling in the Torah scroll
We read it; the way the word is read out loud
Her libation; feminine form, pointing to the מנחה
His libation; masculine form, pointing to the lamb

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think there are two different words in the פסוק. It is one word: spelled one way and read another, and the גמרא learns from both.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: It is written 've-niskah' (and her libation),
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:13. 'Her' is feminine, matching the word מנחה.

phrases.english: and we read it 've-nisko' (and his libation).

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב ״וְנִסְכָּהּ״, וְקָרֵינַן ״וְנִסְכּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 by pointing to the written and read forms of the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word is written as feminine (the מנחה's oil) and read as masculine (the lamb's wine), linking the two.

steps.title: The oil is measured like the wine
steps.stepSummary: Because one word covers both, the oil of the מנחה is a quarter הין, just like the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The 'libation' of the מנחה (the oil) is like the 'libation' of the lamb (the wine). Just as the wine is a quarter, so the oil is also a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר spells out the lesson of the double reading. The oil gets the same measure as the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly says the wine is a quarter הין. Since the same word stands for both the oil and the wine, the oil gets that same quarter הין. So even though the flour is doubled, the oil is not.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? Introduces the explanation
A quarter (here, a quarter of a הין)

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר lamb's מנחה has double flour, but the oil and the wine both stay at the normal quarter הין. This is learned from 'ונסכה' (written) and 'ונסכו' (read).

phrases.english: How so? The 'libation' of the meal offering is like the 'libation' of wine:
just as the wine is a quarter,
so too the oil is also a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? ״נִסְכָּהּ״ דְּמִנְחָה כְּ״נִסְכּוֹ״ דְּיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical rule out of the reading in Step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The oil of the עומר lamb's מנחה is a quarter הין, the same as its wine, and is not doubled.

steps.title: A מצורע's אשם slaughtered for the wrong purpose still needs נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו still requires its נסכים, or else it would be disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: An אשם מצורע that was slaughtered שלא לשמו still requires נסכים. Because if you do not say so, you have disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new related topic. רבי יוחנן rules about an אשם מצורע that was slaughtered with the wrong intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם מצורע is special because it comes with נסכים, unlike a regular אשם. Even when slaughtered שלא לשמו, it is still an אשם מצורע and must keep its נסכים. Bringing it without them would treat it as a different קרבן, and that would make it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering a מצורע brings when he becomes pure
Not for its own sake; slaughtered with the intention of a different קרבן
Requires נסכים: the accompanying מנחה and wine
You have disqualified it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general idea: a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמו keeps the special requirements of what it was set aside for. The next step tests that idea on the עומר lamb.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: A leper's guilt offering
that one slaughtered not for its own sake requires libations,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן – פְּסַלְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: for if you do not say so, you have disqualified it.
phrases.notes: Without נסכים you would be treating it as a different kind of קרבן, and that makes it invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related topic about the extra items that come with a קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו still requires נסכים, because without them it would be disqualified.

steps.title: Then the עומר lamb should keep its doubled מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר גדא challenges: by the same logic, an עומר lamb slaughtered שלא לשמו should still need a doubled מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר גדא objects: If so, a lamb that comes with the עומר that was slaughtered שלא לשמו should have its מנחה doubled. Because if you do not say so, you have disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא בר גדא attacks רבי יוחנן's reasoning. He applies the same logic to the עומר lamb from earlier in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said a special קרבן keeps its special requirements even when slaughtered שלא לשמו. The עומר lamb's special requirement is a doubled מנחה. So the same logic would force us to say it still needs double flour, which רב מנשיא presents as a problem with רבי יוחנן's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; introduces a challenge
If so, then...; shows where an argument would lead

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Gadda objects to this:
If that is so,
a lamb that comes with the omer
that one slaughtered not for its own sake,
its meal offering should be doubled,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן – פְּסַלְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: for if you do not say so, you have disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's reasoning in Step 19 by applying it to the עומר lamb.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reasoning that a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמו keeps its special requirements.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reasoning is right, the עומר lamb slaughtered שלא לשמו would still need a doubled מנחה. רב מנשיא presents this result as a problem with the reasoning.

steps.title: The challenge continues with the morning and afternoon תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר גדא adds two more cases. If a תמיד of the morning or afternoon was slaughtered שלא לשמו, it should still need its special wood arrangement, or else we have disqualified it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the morning תמיד that was slaughtered not for its own sake should still need two logs of wood brought by one כהן, because if you don't say so, you have disqualified it. And the afternoon תמיד that was slaughtered not for its own sake should still need two logs brought by two כהנים, because if you don't say so, you have disqualified it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא בר גדא is still attacking רבי יוחנן's rule. He is adding two more cases that should follow the same logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said a wrong-intent אשם מצורע still needs its נסכים, or else it would be disqualified. Using that same reasoning, the morning and afternoon תמיד should keep their own special wood rules even when slaughtered שלא לשמו. The point of the attack is that רבי יוחנן did not mention these cases, so it looks like his reasoning is not applied consistently.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily morning communal offering
The daily afternoon communal offering
Logs of wood placed on the altar fire

phrases.aramaic: וְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: And the morning daily offering that one slaughtered not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: יְהֵא טָעוּן שְׁנֵי גְזִירִין בְּכֹהֵן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: should require two logs of wood by one priest,
phrases.notes: These are the logs put on the altar fire with the morning תמיד. In the morning, one כהן carries both of them.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן – פְּסַלְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: for if you do not say so, you have disqualified it.

phrases.aramaic: וְתָמִיד שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: And the afternoon daily offering that one slaughtered not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: יְהֵא טָעוּן שְׁנֵי גְזִירִין בִּשְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים,
phrases.english: should require two logs of wood by two priests,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן – פְּסַלְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: for if you do not say so, you have disqualified it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Continuation of the קשיא from step 20
steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more cases to רב מנשיא בר גדא's challenge from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו still needs its נסכים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'otherwise you disqualified it' is a good reason, it should apply to every offering with special extra requirements. Yet רבי יוחנן mentioned only the אשם מצורע.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יוחנן agrees and just mentioned one example
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that all of these cases are true. אביי explains that רבי יוחנן simply mentioned one of them as an example.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. Rather, אביי said: he mentioned one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by agreeing with it. All the cases really do follow רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that if רבי יוחנן said nothing about the other cases, he must disagree with them. אביי says that assumption is wrong. רבי יוחנן holds the same rule for the עומר lamb and the תמיד, and he picked the אשם מצורע only as a sample case.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so. The גמרא accepts the point of the challenge.
He mentioned one of them, as an example

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so,
rather, Abaye said:
He mentioned one of them.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן. He named only the אשם מצורע, but the others work the same way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: חֲדָא מִינַּיְיהוּ נְקַט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב מנשיא בר גדא's challenge from steps 20-21 by agreeing with it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge's conclusion and explains why רבי יוחנן left it out: he gave only one example.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבי יוחנן mentioned only the אשם מצורע, he must not apply his rule to the עומר lamb or the תמיד.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's rule applies to all these cases. He just mentioned one of them.

steps.title: רבי אבא begins a different answer: the other cases are עולות
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא starts another way to answer. The other offerings in the challenge are all עולות, so they are different from the אשם מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: It makes sense regarding those, because they are burnt offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is opening a second answer that is different from אביי's. This line is only the setup, and his full reason continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepted that all the cases are the same. רבי אבא instead limits רבי יוחנן's rule to the אשם מצורע. He points out that the עומר lamb and the תמיד are עולות, and he is getting ready to explain why that makes them different from an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense regarding... This opens a contrast: one case is fine, but another is different.
Burnt offerings, which are burned completely on the altar
Those, meaning the other cases that were just listed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אבא agrees with אביי. אביי says all the cases are the same, while רבי אבא is about to show that the עולות are different from the אשם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Granted, these, they are burnt offerings,
phrases.notes: "These" means the עומר lamb and the two תמיד cases from the challenge. All of them are עולות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָנָךְ, עוֹלוֹת נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from אביי's in step 22. It begins to separate the עולות from the אשם מצורע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between the cases: the offerings in the challenge are עולות, unlike the אשם מצורע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עומר lamb and the תמיד should follow the same logic as the אשם מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולות are in a different category, so רבי יוחנן's rule does not have to extend to them. The full reason continues in the next part of the גמרא.
